subject: Observability Concierge: workflow, SLA exceptions, and per-route cost drilldowns
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability Concierge: workflow, SLA exceptions, and per-route cost drilldowns

Hey team —

Following up from last week's product-engr sync: Acme asked for a single-pane "Observability Concierge" that surfaces per-route cost and tail-latency signals, highlights routes with SLA exposure, and generates a prioritized list of mitigations (e.g., increase cache, pin quantized variant, throttle bulk callers). They want something they can hand to their Ops on-call.

I put together a short deck (attached) with an example concierge flow and an initial SLA matrix. High-level asks:
- A scannable per-route card (cost delta, p95/p99, traffic trend)
- Action suggestions ranked by estimated savings and risk
- Ability to attach a canary/rollback policy to a suggested mitigation

Questions for infra/engineers: is the data we need (per-route token counts, model variant used, cache hit rate, p99 latency) already accessible in the events store at 1-min granularity? If not, what gaps and ETA to populate them?

Can we target a prototype (UI + lightweight backend that uses sampled telemetry) for the customer pilot by 9/24?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Manager, Console 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: observability_concierge_pptx_v1.pptx, sla_matrix.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability Concierge: workflow, SLA exceptions, and per-route cost drilldowns

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Following up from last week's product-engr sync: Acme asked for a single-pane "Observability Concierge"...

Quick notes from infra: we have per-request metadata (route id, model variant, token counts) in the telemetry pipeline, but two caveats:
1) Cache hit rate is sampled at 10% by default; we can increase sampling to 100% for a given tenant but it will increase ingestion cost.
2) The events store currently only materializes per-route p99 rollups on a 5-min window; we can add a 1-min rollup but it requires a small infra change and about ~2 weeks QA.

For the prototype, I propose: use 10% sampling + model-variant attribution + synthetic estimation for cache impact (estimate savings when cache_hit_rate goes from x to y). If the customer pilot needs exact numbers, we can scope a tenant-specific sampling ramp.

Also: we should define the "action suggestion" priorities algorithm. Is it strictly cost-first, or do we weight SLA exposure higher?

I can spin up a stub backend that reads sampled telemetry and generates simple heuristics for suggestion scoring. ETA for prototype backend: 3 weeks (9/20).

- Marcus
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability Concierge: workflow, SLA exceptions, and per-route cost drilldowns

Thanks Marcus — good call on sampling. A few product constraints to lock down before we prototype: 

1) Priority model for suggestions: weight SLA exposure (p99 breaches) x2, cost delta x1.5, and churn risk (routes with recent schema or prompt changes) x1.2. We'll make the weights configurable per-customer.

2) User flows:
   - "Investigate" opens trace + recent payload samples (redacted)
   - "Apply" creates a canary policy (auto-deploy to 10% of traffic for 30m) + optional rollback
   - "Export" generates a one-page incident summary (p95/p99 trend, estimated dollars saved, action taken) for CS/Customer Ops

3) UX: keep cards compact; show three suggested actions max, with an "expand" option for deeper detail.

Acme specifically asked that the concierge be able to produce an "SLA exception justification" export they can use for internal audits — that drives the need for trace links and non-sampled evidence. If we rely on sampling, we should add a "request higher fidelity" button that triggers temporary sampling and collects the evidence with an auditable log.

Can we add a ticket to track the sampling ramp workflow and an audit log entry in the events store when an on-demand ramp happens? That will be important for compliance teams.

I can draft the UX flows this afternoon and will drop a link to the Figma. Naomi, will coordinate pilot acceptance criteria with Acme.

— Jasmine
Principal Product Manager, Observability

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Caroline Park <caroline@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability Concierge: workflow, SLA exceptions, and per-route cost drilldowns

Thanks all — that aligns well. Quick summary / next steps so it's actionable: 

1) Marcus: prototype backend (sampled telemetry + heuristic scorer) — target 9/20. Please include a switch to trigger temporary 100% sampling for a given tenant (logs an audit event).
2) Jasmine: UX flows + Figma mockups for compact route cards + export template — target 9/10.
3) Marissa (CS): draft pilot acceptance criteria and runbook for the Acme Ops team (what counts as "accepted") — target 9/15.
4) Naomi: coordinate with Acme on acceptance criteria and schedule a pilot kickoff the week of 9/27.

Caroline — looping you in; can you confirm Acme's priority is 1) reliable p99 detection, 2) minimal false positives on suggestions, and 3) an export suitable for audit? If yes we'll start the pilot cadence and share the Figma early next week.

If no objections, I'll create linked Jira tickets under OBS and schedule a 30-min sync for 9/7 to align on edge-cases (multi-tenant sampling, billing signal attribution).

Best,
Naomi
Sr. Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference
